---
title: "Using the CLI"
description: "How to use Flower on the command-line."
order: 1
---

`seedcase-flower` is designed to provide a friendly user experience from
the command line. The CLI has commands for both viewing a building
documentation from a Data Package's metadata. The general pattern for
how to use seedcase-flower from the CLI is:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
seedcase-flower COMMAND [ARGS] [OPTIONS]
```

To get started, try calling the program without any commands, arguments,
or options by typing `seedcase-flower` and pressing enter. This is the
same as invoking the `--help` flag and will show the following text:

```{bash filename="Terminal"}
#| echo: false
seedcase-flower
```

## Viewing Data Package metadata

To view the metadata of a Data Package directly in the terminal, you can
use the `view` command like so:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
seedcase-flower view
```

As you can see, the `view` command displays the metadata in an easy to
read format that is optimized for display directly in the terminal. By
default, `view` will look for a `datapackage.json` file in the current
directory, but you can specify a different path if desired:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
seedcase-flower view another/directory/datapackage.json
```

It is also possible to point flower to a Data Package that is available
online. To do this, you can provide the full URL to the remote
`datapackage.json`, e.g.

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
seedcase-flower view https://raw.githubusercontent.com/seedcase-project/example-seed-beetle/refs/heads/main/datapackage.json
```

For files that reside on GitHub, you can use the `gh:` prefix as
a shortcut. For example, the long URL above can be shortened to the
following:

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
seedcase-flower view gh:seedcase-project/example-seed-beetle
```

<!--TODO should we includ output for all of these commands? collapsed by default -->

If you would like to customize the style of how the metadata is
displayed, you can use the `--style` flag. This option allows you to
format the output with any of [the built-in styles](../design/interface/outputs.html#built-in-styles):

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
seedcase-flower view --style quarto-resource-listing gh:seedcase-project/example-seed-beetle
```

For more details about what you can do with `view`, see `seedcase-flower
view --help`.
